questions.explanation_en: As a medium of circulation money mediates the simultaneous act of sale and purchase (commodity - money - commodity). Keeping gold is accumulation, a price tag is the measure of value, and deferred wages illustrate money as a means of payment.

questions.text_en: Money functions as a means of payment primarily when:
options: tovarlar bevosita boshqa tovarlarga ayirboshlansa
mahsulot qiymati narx birliklarida o'lchansa
tangalar metal tarkibi uchun eritib yuborilsa
qarz yoki maosh majburiyati keyinroq to'lansa
options_ru: товары обмениваются прямо на другие товары
стоимость выпуска измеряется в единицах цен
монеты переплавляются ради металла в них
долг или обязательство по оплате гасится позже
options_en: goods are exchanged directly for other goods
the value of output is measured in price units
coins are melted down for their metal content
a debt or wage obligation is settled later
questions.explanation_en: The means-of-payment function appears where the movement of goods and the movement of money are separated in time, as in credit sales, wages, taxes and rent. Direct barter excludes money altogether, measuring value in prices is a different function, and melting coins is not a monetary function at all.

questions.text_en: The function of money as a store of value (accumulation) requires that money:
options: markaziy bank ruxsat bergan eng yuqori tezlikda aylanishi
har bir xorijiy savdo sherigi tomonidan ham qabul qilinishi
saqlanib turgan vaqtida xarid qobiliyatini yo'qotmasligi
faqat metall tangalar shaklida davlat tomonidan chiqarilishi
options_ru: обращались так быстро, как позволяет центральный банк
принимались также каждым зарубежным торговым партнёром
сохраняли покупательную способность в период хранения
выпускались только в виде металлических монет страны
options_en: circulate as rapidly as the central bank permits
be accepted by every foreign trading partner too
retain its purchasing power while it is held
be issued only in the form of metal coins
questions.explanation_en: Money can serve as a store of value only if it holds its purchasing power over time; high inflation destroys this function and pushes people into other assets. Rapid circulation is the opposite of accumulation, foreign acceptance relates to world money, and the metallic form is historical rather than necessary.

questions.text_en: The function of world money means that money:
options: bitta zavod ichida sarflangan mehnat vaqtini o'lchaydi
xalqaro savdoda hisob-kitob va zaxira vazifasini bajaradi
har bir markaziy bank tomonidan teng miqdorda chop etiladi
davlat chegarasidan o'tishi bilan butun qiymatini yo'qotadi
options_ru: измеряют рабочее время, затраченное внутри одного завода
служат расчётам и резервам в международной торговле стран
печатаются в равных объёмах каждым центральным банком мира
теряют всякую стоимость при переходе государственной границы
options_en: measures the labour time spent inside one factory
serves settlements and reserves in international trade
is printed in equal amounts by every central bank
loses all value once it crosses a state border
questions.explanation_en: World money is money functioning beyond national borders as a means of international settlement and as a reserve asset, a role played today by a few key currencies. Measuring labour inside a firm is not a monetary function, central banks issue independently, and convertible currency keeps value across borders.

questions.text_en: Which sequence correctly reflects the historical evolution of money?
options: Tovar puli, metall puli, qog'oz puli, kredit puli
Kredit puli, qog'oz puli, metall puli, tovar puli
Qog'oz puli, tovar puli, kredit puli, metall puli
Metall puli, kredit puli, tovar puli, qog'oz puli
options_ru: Товарные деньги, металлические, бумажные, кредитные
Кредитные деньги, бумажные, металлические, товарные
Бумажные деньги, товарные, кредитные, металлические
Металлические деньги, кредитные, товарные, бумажные
options_en: Commodity money, metallic money, paper money, credit money
Credit money, paper money, metallic money, commodity money
Paper money, commodity money, credit money, metallic money
Metallic money, credit money, commodity money, paper money
questions.explanation_en: Money historically developed from ordinary commodities (cattle, salt, furs) to metal coins, then to paper notes representing metal, and finally to credit and electronic money. The other sequences invert or scramble this order, placing later forms before the earlier ones from which they grew.

questions.text_en: A defining feature of commodity money is that:
options: uning nominal qiymati hukumat qarori bilan belgilanadi
u faqat tijorat banklari yozuvlari shaklida mavjud bo'ladi
uning materiali pul vazifasidan tashqari ham qiymatga ega
u emitent bank tomonidan cheksiz miqdorda yaratilishi mumkin
options_ru: его номинал устанавливается решением правительства
он существует лишь как записи в книгах банков страны
его материал имеет ценность помимо денежного применения
он может создаваться банком-эмитентом без всяких границ
options_en: its face value is fixed by a government decision
it exists only as records in commercial bank ledgers
its own material has value apart from its monetary use
it can be created without limit by the issuing bank
questions.explanation_en: Commodity money (grain, salt, gold) is valuable as a commodity in its own right, so its monetary value is backed by its own use value. Decreed face value and unlimited creation describe fiat money, while ledger records describe deposit or credit money.

questions.text_en: Modern fiat money derives its acceptability mainly from:
options: har bir birlik ortidagi oltin zaxiralaridan
ishlatilgan qog'oz va bo'yoqning o'z qiymatidan
banknot chop etishga ketgan mehnat soatlaridan
davlat hokimiyati va jamoatning unga ishonchidan
options_ru: золотых резервов, стоящих за каждой единицей
собственной ценности бумаги и краски на них
часов труда, затраченных на печать банкнот
власти государства и доверия к ней общества
options_en: the gold reserves held behind each issued unit
the intrinsic worth of the paper and ink used
the labour hours spent printing every banknote
state authority and public confidence in it
questions.explanation_en: Fiat money has negligible intrinsic value and no gold backing; it circulates because the state declares it legal tender and because the public trusts that others will accept it. The cost of paper, ink and printing labour is trivial compared with the face value.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is an example of credit money?
options: Og'irligi muhrlangan holda zarb etilgan oltin tanga
Keyinroq to'lanishi uchun berilgan veksel hujjati
Bir vaqtlar bevosita barterda ishlatilgan tuz bo'lagi
Budjetga to'lov qilinganini tasdiqlovchi soliq tilxati
options_ru: Золотая монета с отчеканенным на ней весом металла
Вексель, выданный с условием оплаты в будущем сроке
Брусок соли, когда-то служивший в прямом обмене
Налоговая квитанция, подтверждающая платёж в бюджет
options_en: A gold coin minted with its weight stamped on it
A bill of exchange issued to be paid at a later date
A bar of salt once used in direct barter deals
A tax receipt proving a payment to the budget
questions.explanation_en: Credit money arises from debt obligations that circulate in place of cash: bills of exchange, banknotes, cheques and deposit transfers. A gold coin is metallic money, salt is commodity money, and a tax receipt is only documentary evidence of a completed payment.

questions.text_en: Which set of properties makes a good suitable to serve as money?
options: Chidamlilik, bo'linuvchanlik, tashish qulayligi, cheklanganlik
Tez buziluvchanlik, bo'linmaslik, og'irlik va mo'l-ko'llik
Mo'rtlik, har bir birlikning noyobligi, cheksiz emissiya
Harakatsizlik, yuqori saqlash xarajati, mavsumiy mavjudlik
options_ru: Долговечность, делимость, портативность, ограниченность
Скоропортящесть, неделимость, тяжесть и изобилие блага
Хрупкость, уникальность каждой единицы, эмиссия без границ
Неподвижность, дорогое хранение, сезонная доступность
options_en: Durability, divisibility, portability and limited supply
Perishability, indivisibility, heaviness and abundance
Fragility, uniqueness of each unit and unlimited issue
Immobility, high storage cost and seasonal availability
questions.explanation_en: A monetary good must keep its physical form, split into small units, be easy to carry, be uniform and be relatively scarce, which is why precious metals were chosen historically. Each distractor lists the opposite qualities, which would make a good unusable as money.

questions.text_en: Gresham's law states that in circulation:
options: yaxshi pul yomon pulni muomaladan asta siqib chiqaradi
pul massasi doimo real mahsulotdan tezroq o'sib boradi
yomon pul yaxshi pulni muomaladan siqib chiqaradi
narxlar pul miqdori o'zgarishiga darhol moslashadi
options_ru: хорошие деньги постепенно вытесняют плохие из оборота
денежная масса всегда растёт быстрее реального выпуска
плохие деньги вытесняют хорошие деньги из обращения
цены мгновенно реагируют на изменение массы денег
options_en: good money gradually drives bad money out of use
money supply always grows faster than real output
bad money tends to drive good money out of use
prices adjust instantly to any change in money
questions.explanation_en: When two kinds of money circulate at the same legal rate, people spend the depreciated (bad) money and hoard or export the full-value (good) money, so bad money stays in circulation. Option 0 reverses the law, while options 1 and 3 state unrelated monetary propositions.

questions.text_en: In the equation of exchange MV = PQ, the symbol V stands for:
options: sotilgan barcha tovarlarning o'rtacha narx darajasi
pul massasining muomalada aylanish tezligi darajasi
ayirboshlangan tovar va xizmatlarning real hajmi
aholi qo'lida bo'lgan pul massasining umumiy miqdori
options_ru: средний уровень цен всех проданных в стране товаров
скорость обращения денежной массы в экономике страны
реальный объём обмениваемых товаров и услуг в стране
общее количество денег, находящихся на руках у людей
options_en: the average price level of all the goods sold here
the velocity of circulation of the money stock
the real volume of goods and services traded here
the total quantity of money held by the public
questions.explanation_en: In Fisher's equation of exchange M is the money stock, V its velocity of circulation, P the price level and Q the real volume of transactions. Options 0, 2 and 3 name P, Q and M respectively, so they identify the other three variables of the same equation.

questions.text_en: Which monetary aggregate contains the narrowest and most liquid part of the money supply?
options: M0, banklardan tashqarida muomaladagi naqd puldan iborat
M1, naqd pulga barcha uzoq muddatli depozitlarni qo'shadi
M2, faqat davlat obligatsiyalari zaxirasini qamrab oladi
M3, faqat xorijiy valyuta zaxiralarini o'z ichiga oladi
options_ru: M0 — наличные деньги в обращении вне банковской системы
M1 — наличные плюс все долгосрочные вклады в банках
M2 — только запасы государственных облигаций страны
M3 — исключительно резервы иностранной валюты страны
options_en: M0, consisting of cash in circulation outside the banks
M1, which adds all long-term bank deposits to the cash
M2, which covers only the government bond holdings
M3, which includes solely the foreign currency reserves
questions.explanation_en: M0 is cash in circulation and is the narrowest and most liquid aggregate; broader aggregates add progressively less liquid items. M1 adds only demand deposits rather than long-term ones, and M2 and M3 are broader aggregates, not bond or reserve lists.

questions.text_en: The liquidity of an asset means its ability to be:
options: uzoq vaqt jismoniy yo'qotishlarsiz saqlab turilishi imkoni
shu sanoat firmasi tomonidan tezda qayta ishlab chiqarilishi
qiymatini deyarli yo'qotmasdan tez naqd pulga aylantirilishi
boshqa o'xshash aktivlarga qaraganda past stavkada soliqlanishi
options_ru: долго храниться без каких-либо физических потерь
быстро вновь произведённым той же фирмой отрасли
быстро превращённым в наличные почти без потерь
обложенным налогом по более низкой ставке, чем иные
options_en: stored for a long period without any physical loss
produced again quickly by the same industrial firm
converted into cash quickly with little loss of value
taxed at a lower rate than other comparable assets
questions.explanation_en: Liquidity measures how fast and how cheaply an asset can be turned into means of payment, which is why cash is perfectly liquid and real estate is not. Durability, reproducibility and tax treatment are different asset characteristics that do not define liquidity.

questions.text_en: In commodity-money relations, price is understood as:
options: mahsulotda mujassam bo'lgan mehnat soatlari miqdori
tovar qiymatining pul shaklidagi ifodalanishi
tushum va umumiy xarajatlar o'rtasidagi tafovut
maosh sifatida to'langan milliy daromad ulushi
options_ru: количество часов труда, воплощённых в продукте
денежное выражение стоимости данного товара
разница между выручкой и общими затратами фирмы
доля национального дохода, выплаченная как плата
options_en: the quantity of labour hours embodied in a product
the monetary expression of the value of a commodity
the difference between revenue and total costs
the share of national income paid out as wages
questions.explanation_en: Price is value expressed in money, so it may deviate from value under the influence of supply and demand. Embodied labour is value itself, revenue minus costs is profit, and the wage share is a distributional category.

questions.text_en: The law of value requires that commodities be exchanged:
options: rejalashtirish idorasi doimiy belgilagan narxlarda
faqat qat'iy teng jismoniy miqdorlarda almashtirilishi
kuchli tomon majburlagan har qanday narx bo'yicha
ularga ijtimoiy zarur mehnat miqdoriga muvofiq ravishda
options_ru: по ценам, навсегда установленным плановым органом
только в строго равных физических количествах благ
по любой цене, навязанной более сильной стороной
в соответствии с общественно необходимым трудом
options_en: at prices fixed permanently by the planning agency
only in strictly equal physical quantities of goods
at whatever price the stronger party can impose
in accordance with the labour socially needed for them
questions.explanation_en: The law of value means exchange of equivalents: goods trade in proportion to the socially necessary labour embodied in them, and price deviations around value regulate the flow of resources between branches. Equal physical quantities, administered prices and coercive pricing all contradict equivalent exchange.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is NOT a function of price in a market economy?
options: Bitimlar to'g'risida ma'lumot berish va hisob yuritish
Ishlab chiqaruvchilarni xarajatni qisqartirishga undash
Resurslarni raqobatlashuvchi tarmoqlar o'rtasida taqsimlash
Har bir firmaga teng foyda olishni kafolatlab berish
options_ru: Информирование о сделках и ведение их учёта в хозяйстве
Побуждение производителей снижать издержки и новшества
Распределение ресурсов между конкурирующими отраслями
Гарантия равной прибыли каждой фирме в любом периоде
options_en: Providing information and accounting for transactions
Stimulating producers to cut costs and innovate more
Distributing resources among competing branches
Guaranteeing every firm an equal profit each period
questions.explanation_en: Prices inform, measure, stimulate, distribute resources and balance supply with demand, but they cannot guarantee equal profits; on the contrary, differences in profit are the signal that moves capital between branches. The other three options are standard price functions.

questions.text_en: A sustained rise in the general price level means that money:
options: vaqt o'tishi bilan xarid qobiliyatining bir qismini yo'qotadi
vaqt o'tishi bilan qo'shimcha xarid qobiliyatiga ega bo'ladi
muomala vositasi vazifasini bajarishdan butunlay to'xtaydi
iqtisodiyotdagi yagona jamg'arish vositasiga aylanib qoladi
options_ru: со временем теряет часть своей покупательной способности
со временем приобретает дополнительную покупательную силу
полностью перестаёт служить средством обращения в стране
становится единственным средством накопления в хозяйстве
options_en: loses part of its purchasing power over time
gains additional purchasing power over time
ceases to serve as a medium of circulation
becomes the only store of value in economy
questions.explanation_en: Inflation means that the same nominal sum buys fewer goods, so purchasing power falls; this weakens, in particular, the store-of-value function. Purchasing power cannot rise during inflation, money normally keeps circulating, and inflation makes money a worse rather than the only store of value.

chapters.title_uz: Bozor iqtisodiyoti va unga o'tish yo'lları
chapters.title_ru: Рыночная экономика и пути перехода к ней
chapters.title_en: Market economy and ways of transition to it

questions.text_en: In economic theory, a market is best defined as:
options: davlat amaldorlari bitimlarni qayd etadigan bino
rejalashtirish vazirligi tasdiqlagan narxlar ro'yxati
xaridorlar va sotuvchilar o'rtasidagi munosabatlar tizimi
firmalarning zararlarini qoplaydigan maxsus jamg'arma
options_ru: здание, где чиновники регистрируют все сделки
перечень цен, утверждённый плановым министерством
система отношений между покупателями и продавцами
фонд, возмещающий фирмам понесённые ими убытки
options_en: a building where state officials register all deals
a list of prices approved by the planning ministry
a system of relations between buyers and sellers
a fund that compensates firms for their losses
questions.explanation_en: A market is not a physical place but the whole set of exchange relations through which buyers and sellers coordinate their decisions. A trading hall is only one possible form, an approved price list belongs to administrative planning, and a compensation fund is a budgetary instrument.

questions.text_en: Which combination best characterises a market economy?
options: Davlat mulki, direktiv rejalar va qat'iy davlat narxlari
Xususiy mulk, erkin narx shakllanishi va ochiq raqobat
Kolxozlar, barter savdosi va cheklangan iste'mol tizimi
Yopiq chegaralar, yagona ishlab chiqaruvchi, foyda kafolati
options_ru: Госсобственность, директивные планы и твёрдые цены
Частная собственность, свободные цены, конкуренция
Колхозы, обмен товарами и нормированное потребление
Закрытые границы, единый производитель, гарантии
options_en: State ownership, directive plans and fixed state prices
Private ownership, free pricing and open competition
Collective farms, barter trade and rationed consumption
Closed borders, single producer and guaranteed profits
questions.explanation_en: The basic institutional pillars of a market economy are private property, freely formed prices, competition and freedom of enterprise. The other combinations describe a command economy, a semi-natural rationed economy and a closed monopolised system respectively.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is a genuine function of the market mechanism?
options: Uy xo'jaliklari o'rtasidagi daromad farqlarini yo'q qilish
Har bir vaqtda mehnatning to'liq bandligini kafolatlash
Davlat xarajatisiz barcha jamoat tovarlarini ta'minlash
Narx o'zgarishi orqali tanqislik haqida signal berish
options_ru: Устранение всех различий в доходах между хозяйствами
Гарантия полной занятости труда в каждый момент времени
Поставка всех общественных благ без расходов бюджета
Сигнал о редкости производителям через изменение цен
options_en: Eliminating all income differences between households
Guaranteeing full employment of labour at every moment
Supplying all public goods without any state spending
Signalling scarcity to producers through price changes
questions.explanation_en: The informational and regulating function of the market works through prices, which tell producers where goods are scarce and resources are needed. Markets do not level incomes, do not guarantee full employment, and systematically under-provide public goods.

questions.text_en: Adam Smith's idea of the 'invisible hand' suggests that:
options: shaxsiy manfaat yo'lidagi harakat umumiy foyda keltiradi
markaziy rejalashtiruvchi barcha tanlovni boshqarishi kerak
erkin savdo doimo bir tomonni ancha kambag'al qoldiradi
narxlar ishlab chiqaruvchilar kelishuvi bilan belgilanadi
options_ru: действия ради личной выгоды служат и общему благу
центральный плановик должен направлять все решения
свободная торговля всегда делает одну сторону беднее
цены следует устанавливать по сговору производителей
options_en: self-interested actions can serve the common good
a central planner must direct all private choices
free trade always leaves one partner much poorer
prices should be set by agreement among producers
questions.explanation_en: Smith argued that competition channels private self-interest into socially useful outcomes without conscious direction. Central planning is the opposite idea, mutually voluntary trade normally benefits both parties, and price agreements among producers are collusion, which destroys the mechanism.

questions.text_en: Consumer sovereignty in a market economy means that:
options: iste'molchilar mahalliy tovarlarni sotib olishga majbur
davlat uy xo'jaliklari qanday tovar olishini hal qiladi
iste'molchi xarajatlari firmalar ishlab chiqarishini belgilaydi
ishlab chiqaruvchilar narxni cheklovsiz oshirishi mumkin
options_ru: потребители обязаны по закону покупать местные товары
государство решает, какие блага могут купить семьи
расходы потребителей определяют, что выпускают фирмы
производители могут повышать цены без всяких границ
options_en: consumers are legally obliged to buy domestic goods
the state decides which goods households may purchase
consumer spending choices guide what firms produce
producers may raise prices without any limitation
questions.explanation_en: Consumer sovereignty means that the structure of production follows the structure of consumer demand, since firms that ignore buyers' preferences make losses. Legal purchase obligations and state allocation of goods belong to a command system, and competition limits how far prices can be raised.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is a recognised advantage of a market economy?
options: U barcha fuqarolar daromadini avtomatik tenglashtiradi
U narx signallari orqali resurslarni samarali taqsimlaydi
U shartnomalar bo'yicha huquqiy qoidalar zaruratini yo'qotadi
U monopoliya hokimiyati paydo bo'lishini butunlay to'xtatadi
options_ru: Она автоматически уравнивает доходы всех граждан страны
Она эффективно размещает ресурсы через сигналы рыночных цен
Она устраняет нужду в любых правовых нормах о договорах
Она полностью предотвращает появление монопольной власти
options_en: It automatically equalises the incomes of all citizens
It allocates resources efficiently through price signals
It removes the need for any legal rules on contracts
It prevents the emergence of monopoly power entirely
questions.explanation_en: Allocative efficiency through decentralised price signals, together with strong incentives to innovate, is the central advantage of markets. Markets tend to widen rather than equalise incomes, they depend heavily on contract law, and they can generate monopoly power on their own.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is a typical disadvantage of a pure market economy?
options: Har bir tarmoqda iste'mol tovarlarining surunkali tanqisligi
Yangilik kiritishga rag'batning butunlay mavjud emasligi
Sanoatda mehnat unumdorligining doimiy pasayib borishi
Daromad tengsizligi va jamoat tovarlarining yetarsizligi
options_ru: Хронический дефицит потребительских благ во всех отраслях
Полное отсутствие каких-либо стимулов к введению новшеств
Постоянное падение производительности труда в индустрии
Большое неравенство доходов и нехватка общественных благ
options_en: Chronic shortages of consumer goods in every branch
Complete absence of any incentive to innovate at all
Permanently falling labour productivity in industry
Large income inequality and under-supply of public goods
questions.explanation_en: The standard weaknesses of markets are income inequality, unemployment, externalities, under-provision of public goods, monopolisation and cyclical instability. Chronic shortages and weak innovation incentives are characteristic of command economies, and falling productivity is not an inherent market outcome.

questions.text_en: The term 'market failure' refers to a situation where:
options: tarmoqdagi bitta firma qonuniy ravishda bankrot bo'lsa
tovarning bozor narxi o'tgan yildagidan pastga tushsa
erkin bozorlar resurslarni o'zicha samarasiz taqsimlasa
iste'molchilar e'lon qilingan narxda tovar olishdan voz kechsa
options_ru: одна фирма в отрасли юридически становится банкротом
рыночная цена блага падает ниже прошлогоднего уровня
свободные рынки сами размещают ресурсы неэффективно
покупатели отказываются брать блага по объявленным ценам
options_en: a single firm in an industry becomes legally bankrupt
the market price of a good falls below last year's one
free markets allocate resources inefficiently by themselves
consumers refuse to buy goods offered at posted prices
questions.explanation_en: Market failure is the inability of unregulated markets to reach an efficient allocation, as with externalities, public goods, monopoly and asymmetric information. Bankruptcy of one firm, a price fall, or refusal to buy at a given price are normal market outcomes, not failures of the mechanism.

questions.text_en: Public goods are under-provided by the market because they are:
options: iste'molda raqobatsiz va foydalanishda cheklanmaydigan
faqat davlat litsenziyasiga ega firmalar chiqaradigan
doimo chekli xarajatdan ancha yuqori narxda sotiladigan
asosan yuqori daromadli uy xo'jaliklari iste'mol qiladigan
options_ru: неконкурентными в потреблении и неисключаемыми в доступе
выпускаемыми только фирмами с государственной лицензией
всегда продаваемыми по ценам много выше предельных затрат
потребляемыми в основном лишь семьями с высоким доходом
options_en: non-rival in consumption and non-excludable in use
produced only by firms holding a state licence
always sold at prices far above their marginal cost
consumed mainly by high-income households only
questions.explanation_en: Non-rivalry and non-excludability create the free-rider problem: private firms cannot charge users, so they do not supply such goods as national defence or street lighting. Licensing, high mark-ups and the income profile of users are not the defining features of public goods.

questions.text_en: Which case is an example of a negative externality?
options: Firma yaxshi mashina olgach, mahsulot narxini pasaytiradi
Zavod yaqin aholi foydalanadigan daryoni ifloslantiradi
Do'kon eng sodiq xaridorlariga chegirmalar taklif qiladi
Ishchi qayta o'qitilib, so'ng yuqoriroq maosh oladi
options_ru: Фирма снижает цену, купив более совершенные машины
Завод загрязняет реку, которой пользуются жители
Магазин предлагает скидки самым верным покупателям
Работник переучен и затем получает более высокую плату
options_en: A firm lowers its price after buying better machines
A plant pollutes a river used by nearby households
A shop offers discounts to its most loyal customers
A worker is retrained and then earns a higher wage
questions.explanation_en: A negative externality is a cost imposed on third parties who are not part of the transaction, which is exactly what river pollution does. Price cuts, discounts and higher wages after training are all transmitted through the market itself, so they are not external effects.

questions.text_en: In a modern mixed market economy the state mainly:
options: har bir korxona uchun oldindan ishlab chiqarish rejasini belgilaydi
butun ishlab chiqarish kapitaliga bevosita egalik qiladi
har bir iste'mol tovarining chakana narxini qat'iy belgilaydi
jamoat tovarlarini beradi va bozor nuqsonlarini tuzatadi
options_ru: заранее задаёт плановые задания для каждого предприятия страны
напрямую владеет всем запасом производительного капитала
жёстко фиксирует розничную цену каждого потребительского блага
поставляет общественные блага и исправляет провалы рынка
options_en: sets output targets in advance for every single enterprise
owns the whole stock of productive capital directly
fixes the retail price of each consumer good that is sold
supplies public goods and corrects market failures
questions.explanation_en: The modern state provides public goods, regulates monopolies, internalises externalities, redistributes income and stabilises the macroeconomy. Directive output targets, universal state ownership and comprehensive price fixing are features of the command system that mixed economies have abandoned.

questions.text_en: Which group of institutions forms the infrastructure of a market?
options: Banklar, fond birjalari, sug'urta firmalari, mehnat idoralari
Reja qo'mitalari, ta'minot idoralari, karta bo'limlari
Kolxozlar, qishloq kengashlari va davlat omborxonalari
Bojxona punktlari, chegara qo'riqchilari, migratsiya nazorati
options_ru: Банки, фондовые биржи, страховые фирмы, службы труда
Плановые комитеты, органы снабжения, отделы карточек
Колхозы, сельские советы и государственные склады
Таможни, пограничная охрана, миграционные инспекции
options_en: Banks, stock exchanges, insurance firms and labour offices
Planning committees, supply boards and ration departments
Collective farms, village councils and state storehouses
Customs posts, border guards and migration inspectorates
questions.explanation_en: Market infrastructure comprises the institutions that service exchange: banks, exchanges, insurance companies, auditing and consulting firms, employment services and trade intermediaries. The other lists describe planning organs, rural administration under the command system, and border control agencies.

questions.text_en: Markets are classified by the object of trade into markets for:
options: mahalliy, hududiy, milliy va xalqaro bitimlar bozorlari
ulgurji, chakana, mavsumiy va doimiy bitimlar bozorlari
tovarlar, xizmatlar, mehnat, kapital va ma'lumot bozorlari
qonuniy, noqonuniy, nazoratli va erkin bitimlar bozorlari
options_ru: местных, региональных, национальных и мировых сделок
оптовых, розничных, сезонных и постоянных сделок
товаров, услуг, труда, капитала и информации в стране
законных, незаконных, регулируемых и свободных сделок
options_en: local, regional, national and international dealings
wholesale, retail, seasonal and permanent dealings
goods, services, labour, capital and information here
legal, illegal, regulated and deregulated dealings
questions.explanation_en: Classification by object of exchange gives markets for consumer goods, services, labour, capital, land and information. The other options classify markets by geographical scope, by the scale and timing of transactions, and by legal status respectively.

questions.text_en: A market with many small firms selling an identical product and free entry is called:
options: yagona sotuvchi xizmat qiladigan sof monopoliya bozori
firmalar o'rtasida mukammal raqobat mavjud bozor turi
bir necha yirik firma ustunlik qiladigan oligopoliya
tovarning yagona xaridori bo'lgan monopsoniya bozori
options_ru: чистая монополия, обслуживаемая единственным продавцом
рынок совершенной конкуренции между многими фирмами
олигополия, где господствуют несколько крупных фирм
монопсония с единственным покупателем данного блага
options_en: a pure monopoly served by one single seller
a market of perfect competition among firms
an oligopoly dominated by a few large firms
a monopsony with only one buyer of the good
questions.explanation_en: Perfect competition requires many small sellers, a homogeneous product, free entry and exit, and full information, so that no firm can influence price. Monopoly has one seller, oligopoly a few large sellers, and monopsony a single buyer.

questions.text_en: A transition economy is one that is moving from:
options: markazlashgan reja tizimidan bozor tizimi tomon
bozor tizimidan to'liq markaziy rejalashtirishga
agrar tuzilmadan natural xo'jalik tomon o'tishda
monopollashgan tarmoqdan davlat mulki tomon
options_ru: централизованного планирования к рыночной системе страны
рыночной системы к полному центральному планированию
аграрной структуры к натуральному хозяйству страны
монополизированной отрасли к государственной собственности
options_en: a centrally planned system towards a market system
a market system towards complete central planning
an agrarian structure towards a natural economy
a monopolised sector towards full state ownership
questions.explanation_en: Transition economies are those replacing administrative-command coordination with market coordination through liberalisation, privatisation and institution building. Option 1 reverses the direction, while options 2 and 3 describe structural shifts that are not what the term means.

questions.text_en: The 'shock therapy' strategy of transition is characterised by:
options: ko'p o'n yillarga cho'zilgan sekin bosqichma-bosqich islohot
davlat narxlarini saqlab, avval yerni xususiylashtirish
narxlarni tez erkinlashtirish va tezkor ommaviy xususiylashtirish
qisqa bozor davridan keyin markaziy rejani qayta tiklash
options_ru: медленные поэтапные реформы, растянутые на десятилетия
сохранение твёрдых цен при первичной приватизации земли
быстрая либерализация цен и ускоренная приватизация
возврат к центральному плану после краткого рыночного этапа
options_en: slow step-by-step reforms spread over many decades
keeping state prices while privatising land first
rapid price liberalisation and fast mass privatisation
restoring central planning after a short market period
questions.explanation_en: Shock therapy compresses liberalisation, stabilisation and privatisation into a very short period, aiming to make reforms irreversible at the cost of a deep initial fall in output. Option 0 describes the gradual path, and options 1 and 3 describe partial or reversed reform scenarios.

questions.text_en: The gradual (evolutionary) path of transition is distinguished by:
options: davlat narx nazoratini darhol butunlay bekor qilish
barcha tarmoqlarda xususiy mulkni tugatib yuborish
bir yil ichida amalga oshirilgan yagona islohot akti
bosqichli islohot va faol ijtimoiy himoya choralari
options_ru: немедленная отмена всякого государственного контроля цен
упразднение частной собственности во всех отраслях
единый акт реформы, проведённый в течение одного года
поэтапные реформы с активными мерами соцзащиты людей
options_en: an immediate removal of every state price control
the abolition of private property in all branches
a single reform act carried out within one year
staged reforms with active social protection measures
questions.explanation_en: The gradual approach sequences reforms over time, builds market institutions first and cushions the social cost, which reduces the output decline but lengthens the transition. Immediate full liberalisation belongs to shock therapy, and abolishing private property would reverse the transition entirely.

questions.text_en: Privatisation during transition means the transfer of:
options: xususiy aktivlarni davlat mulki tarkibiga o'tkazishni
davlat aktivlarini xususiy shaxslar mulkiga o'tkazishni
davlat qarzini markaziy bankdan aholi zimmasiga o'tkazishni
xorijiy kapitalni milliy zaxira jamg'armasiga o'tkazishni
options_ru: частных активов в собственность государства страны
государственных активов в собственность частных лиц
долга государства от центрального банка к населению
иностранного капитала в национальный резервный фонд
options_en: private assets into the ownership of the state
state assets into the ownership of private agents
public debt from the central bank to households
foreign capital into the national reserve fund
questions.explanation_en: Privatisation creates private owners with an interest in efficiency by selling or distributing state enterprises and property. Option 0 describes nationalisation, the exact opposite, while options 2 and 3 describe debt and reserve operations that have nothing to do with ownership change.

questions.text_en: Price liberalisation in a transition economy means that prices:
options: qonun bilan tanlangan bazis yil darajasida muzlatib qo'yiladi
vazirlik tomonidan har chorakda bir marta qayta hisoblanadi
talab va taklif o'zaro ta'siri natijasida erkin shakllanadi
bekor qilinib, o'rniga tovarlarni karta bilan taqsimlash keladi
options_ru: замораживаются законом на уровне выбранного базового года
пересчитываются министерством один раз в каждом квартале
свободно формируются взаимодействием спроса и предложения
отменяются, а вместо них вводится прямое нормирование благ
options_en: are frozen by law at the level of a chosen base year
are recalculated by the ministry once in each quarter
are formed freely by the interaction of supply and demand
are abolished and replaced by direct rationing of goods
questions.explanation_en: Liberalisation hands price setting over to the market, so that prices can perform their informational and balancing functions and shortages disappear. Freezing, periodic administrative recalculation and rationing are all forms of continued state price control.

questions.text_en: Macroeconomic stabilisation during transition aims mainly at:
options: inflatsiyani jilovlash va budjet muvozanatini tiklash
barcha iste'mol tovarlariga import bojini oshirish
davlat mulkidagi zavodlar sonini kengaytirib borish
valyuta kursini abadiy qat'iy darajada belgilab qo'yish
options_ru: обуздание инфляции и восстановление баланса бюджета
повышение импортных пошлин на все потребительские блага
расширение числа находящихся в госсобственности заводов
навсегда фиксированное закрепление курса национальной валюты
options_en: curbing inflation and restoring the budget balance
raising import tariffs on all the consumer goods
expanding the number of state-owned factories
fixing the national exchange rate level forever
questions.explanation_en: Stabilisation combines tight monetary and fiscal policy to bring inflation down and close the budget deficit, creating the stable environment that markets need. Higher tariffs are protectionism, expanding state ownership contradicts transition, and a permanently fixed exchange rate is not a stabilisation goal in itself.

questions.text_en: A key principle of the Uzbek model of transition to a market economy is that:
options: islohotlar yagona tezkor shok sifatida amalga oshirilishi kerak
davlat iqtisodiyotdan birdaniga butunlay chekinishi kerak
barcha korxonalar avval xorijiy investorlarga sotilishi kerak
davlat asosiy islohotchi bo'lib, ijtimoiy himoyani ta'minlaydi
options_ru: реформы должны проводиться как единый и быстрый шок страны
государство обязано сразу полностью уйти из экономики
все предприятия сначала продаются иностранным инвесторам
государство — главный реформатор, обеспечивающий соцзащиту
options_en: reforms must be carried out as a single rapid shock
the state should withdraw fully from the economy at once
all enterprises must be sold to foreign investors first
the state acts as chief reformer with social protection
questions.explanation_en: The Uzbek model rests on the primacy of economics over politics, the state as the principal reformer, the rule of law, strong social protection and gradual, staged reform. Shock therapy, immediate withdrawal of the state and reliance on foreign buyers are precisely the alternatives this model rejected.

questions.text_en: Demonopolisation of the economy during transition is intended to:
options: kichik firmalarni bir necha yirik davlat konsernlariga qo'shish
monopoliyalarni bo'lish va bozorlarda raqobatni kengaytirish
yagona milliy idoraga eksklyuziv import huquqini berish
yangi xususiy firmalarning tarmoqqa kirishini taqiqlash
options_ru: слить мелкие фирмы в несколько крупных госконцернов
раздробить монополии и расширить конкуренцию рынков
дать единому ведомству исключительное право импорта
запретить вход новых частных фирм в данную отрасль
options_en: merge small firms into a few large state concerns
break up monopolies and widen competition in markets
grant exclusive import rights to one national agency
forbid the entry of new private firms into industry
questions.explanation_en: Command economies left behind giant monopolies, so transition requires splitting them, removing entry barriers and enforcing antimonopoly law to create real competition. The other options would concentrate market power further rather than reduce it.

questions.text_en: Why is building a legal and institutional framework essential in transition?
options: Chunki u davlatga yana barcha narxlarni belgilashga imkon beradi
Chunki u xususiy jamg'armalarga bo'lgan zaruratni yo'q qiladi
Chunki mustahkam mulk huquqi va shartnoma savdoni ta'minlaydi
Chunki u har bir firmaga ijobiy foyda darajasini kafolatlaydi
options_ru: Потому что это позволяет государству вновь задавать цены
Потому что это снимает нужду в частных сбережениях людей
Потому что надёжные права и договоры делают обмен возможным
Потому что это гарантирует каждой фирме положительную прибыль
options_en: Because it allows the state to set all the prices again
Because it removes the need for any private savings
Because secure property rights and contracts enable trade
Because it guarantees every firm a positive profit level
questions.explanation_en: Markets cannot function without enforceable property rights, contract law, courts, accounting standards and a reliable banking system, since these reduce uncertainty and transaction costs. Institutions do not restore administrative pricing, do not replace savings, and cannot guarantee profits to any firm.

questions.text_en: The growth of the shadow economy during transition is usually caused by:
options: kuchsiz institutlar, og'ir soliqlar va yomon huquq nazorati
past inflatsiya, barqaror narxlar va ochiq tashqi savdo
mustahkam mulk huquqi va shaffof soliq yig'imi tizimi
faqat davlat sektorida real maoshning tez o'sib borishi
options_ru: слабые институты, тяжёлые налоги и плохой надзор закона
низкая инфляция, твёрдые цены и открытая внешняя торговля
надёжные права собственности и прозрачный сбор налогов
быстрый рост реальной платы лишь в государственном секторе
options_en: weak institutions, heavy taxes and poor law enforcement
low inflation, stable prices and open foreign trade
strong property rights and transparent tax collection
rapid growth of real wages in the public sector alone
questions.explanation_en: Informal activity expands where the official rules are costly to obey and cheap to break: high tax burdens, excessive regulation and weak enforcement push firms underground. Strong institutions, transparent taxation and macroeconomic stability shrink the shadow sector instead.

questions.text_en: Rapid liberalisation of prices without monetary discipline typically leads to:
options: umumiy narx darajasining darhol pasayib ketishi holatiga
inflatsiyaning keskin o'sishi va real daromad yo'qolishiga
barcha iste'mol bozorlarida tovar ortiqchaligi doimiyligiga
davlat budjetining har yili avtomatik muvozanatlashuviga
options_ru: немедленному падению общего уровня всех цен в стране
резкой вспышке инфляции и потере реальных доходов
постоянному избытку благ на всех потребительских рынках
автоматической ежегодной сбалансированности бюджета
options_en: an immediate fall in the general level of all prices
a sharp burst of inflation and loss of real incomes
a permanent surplus of goods in all consumer markets
an automatic balancing of the state budget each year
questions.explanation_en: Freeing prices while the money supply keeps expanding converts suppressed shortages into open, often very high inflation, which erodes wages and savings. Deflation, permanent surpluses and automatic budget balance are not observed outcomes of uncontrolled liberalisation.

questions.text_en: Why is a social safety net necessary during the transition period?
options: Barcha iste'mol narxlarini oldingi darajada saqlab turish uchun
Xususiylashtirilgan zavodlarda ishdan bo'shatishni taqiqlash uchun
Qayta qurish va ishsizlikdan zarar ko'rganlarni qo'llash uchun
Xorijiy investorlarga aksiya xaridini moliyalashtirish uchun
options_ru: Чтобы сохранить все потребительские цены на прежнем уровне
Чтобы запретить любые увольнения на приватизированных заводах
Чтобы поддержать пострадавших от реструктуризации и потери работы
Чтобы финансировать покупку акций иностранными инвесторами
options_en: To keep all the consumer prices at their previous levels
To forbid any layoffs in the newly privatised factories
To support groups hurt by restructuring and job losses
To finance the purchase of shares by foreign investors
questions.explanation_en: Restructuring inevitably closes unprofitable enterprises and raises unemployment, so targeted benefits, retraining and minimum guarantees are needed to keep reform socially acceptable. Freezing prices or banning layoffs would block the very restructuring that transition requires.

questions.text_en: Competition in a market economy mainly acts as a mechanism that:
options: tarmoqdagi barcha firmalarga bir xil foyda kafolatlaydi
eng yirik firmaga tarmoq hajmini belgilashga yo'l beradi
kuchsiz ishlab chiqaruvchilar uchun bankrotlik xavfini yo'qotadi
firmalarni xarajatni qisqartirish va sifatni oshirishga undaydi
options_ru: гарантирует одинаковую прибыль всем фирмам отрасли
позволяет крупнейшей фирме диктовать объём отрасли
снимает угрозу банкротства для слабых производителей
побуждает фирмы снижать издержки и улучшать качество
options_en: guarantees identical profits to all firms in a branch
allows the largest firm to dictate industry output
removes the risk of bankruptcy for weak producers
pushes firms to cut costs and improve product quality
questions.explanation_en: Competition is the disciplining force of the market: firms that do not reduce costs, innovate and satisfy buyers lose market share and exit. It does not equalise profits, does not hand price-setting power to the largest firm, and increases rather than removes the threat of bankruptcy.

questions.text_en: The law of demand states that, other things equal, a rise in price leads to:
options: tovarga talab qilinadigan miqdorning ortishiga
tovarga talab qilinadigan miqdorning kamayishiga
talab qilinadigan miqdorning umuman o'zgarmasligiga
tovar taklif qilinadigan miqdorning kamayishiga
options_ru: росту величины спроса на этот конкретный товар
падению величины спроса на этот конкретный товар
полному отсутствию изменений в величине спроса
падению величины предложения этого же товара
options_en: a rise in the quantity demanded of the good
a fall in the quantity demanded of the good
no change at all in the quantity demanded
a fall in the quantity supplied of the good
questions.explanation_en: The law of demand expresses the inverse relation between price and quantity demanded, which gives the demand curve its negative slope. Option 0 reverses this relation, option 2 describes perfectly inelastic demand as a general rule, and option 3 confuses demand with supply.

questions.text_en: The downward slope of the demand curve is explained mainly by:
options: ishlab chiqaruvchi firmalarning o'sib boruvchi chekli xarajati
sotuvchi kompaniyaning o'zgarmas pul daromadi darajasi
narx o'zgarishining daromad va o'rin bosish effektlari
yangi firmalarning tarmoqqa erkin kirib kelishi omili
options_ru: ростом предельных издержек у производящих фирм
неизменным денежным доходом продающей компании
эффектами дохода и замещения при изменении цены
свободным входом новых фирм в данную отрасль
options_en: the rising marginal costs faced by producing firms
the fixed money income of each selling company
the income and substitution effects of a price change
the free entry of new firms into this industry
questions.explanation_en: A higher price reduces the real purchasing power of the buyer's income (income effect) and makes substitutes relatively cheaper (substitution effect), so quantity demanded falls; diminishing marginal utility works in the same direction. Rising marginal cost and free entry explain supply, not demand.

questions.text_en: A fall in the price of a good, with all other factors unchanged, causes:
options: mavjud talab chizig'i bo'ylab siljishni keltirib chiqaradi
butun talab chizig'ining o'ngga siljishini keltirib chiqaradi
butun talab chizig'ining chapga siljishini keltirib chiqaradi
faqat taklif chizig'ining vertikal burilishini keltiradi
options_ru: перемещение вдоль существующей кривой спроса
сдвиг всей кривой спроса вправо на графике
сдвиг всей кривой спроса влево на графике
вертикальный поворот только кривой предложения
options_en: a movement along the existing demand curve
a rightward shift of the whole demand curve
a leftward shift of the whole demand curve
a vertical rotation of the supply curve only
questions.explanation_en: A change in the good's own price changes quantity demanded, which is a movement along a given demand curve. Shifts of the whole curve are caused only by non-price determinants such as income, tastes, prices of related goods and expectations.

questions.text_en: Which factor shifts the demand curve rather than causing movement along it?
options: Tovarning o'z bozor narxidagi o'zgarish holati
Tovar hozir sotilayotgan miqdordagi o'zgarish
Chizilgan taklif chizig'i qiyaligidagi o'zgarish
Iste'molchi daromadi va didlaridagi o'zgarish
options_ru: Изменение самой рыночной цены данного блага
Изменение количества, продаваемого сейчас
Изменение наклона построенной кривой предложения
Изменение доходов потребителей и их вкусов
options_en: A change in the market price of the good itself
A change in the quantity the good is sold at now
A change in the slope of the supply curve drawn
A change in consumer incomes and their tastes
questions.explanation_en: Non-price determinants (income, tastes, prices of substitutes and complements, expectations, number of buyers) shift the whole demand schedule. The good's own price and quantity only move the economy along the curve, and the slope of supply does not relocate demand.

questions.text_en: If consumer income rises, the demand for a normal good will:
options: ortadi va talab chizig'i o'ngga siljiydi
kamayadi va talab chizig'i chapga siljiydi
har qanday narxda aynan o'zgarmagan qoladi
oldingi narxda mutlaqo noelastik bo'lib qoladi
options_ru: вырастет, и кривая спроса сдвинется вправо
упадёт, и кривая спроса сдвинется влево
останется точно такой же при любой цене
станет совершенно неэластичным при старой цене
options_en: increase, shifting its demand curve to the right
decrease, shifting its demand curve to the left
stay exactly the same at every possible price
become perfectly inelastic at the former price
questions.explanation_en: For a normal good income and demand move in the same direction, so higher income shifts the demand curve rightward. A leftward shift would indicate an inferior good, while unchanged demand would mean zero income elasticity.

questions.text_en: A good is called inferior when a rise in consumer income leads to:
options: o'sha tovarga talabning proporsional ortishiga
o'sha tovarga talabning umuman o'zgarmasligiga
aynan o'sha tovarga talabning kamayib ketishiga
o'sha tovarning bozor taklifi ortib borishiga
options_ru: пропорциональному росту спроса на это благо
полному отсутствию изменений спроса на него
уменьшению спроса именно на это самое благо
росту рыночного предложения этого же блага
options_en: a proportional rise in the demand for that good
no change whatever in the demand for that good
a decrease in the demand for that particular good
a rise in the market supply of that same good
questions.explanation_en: An inferior good has negative income elasticity: as incomes grow consumers switch to better substitutes, so demand for it falls. A proportional rise characterises a normal good, no change means zero elasticity, and supply is determined by producers rather than by buyers' income.

questions.text_en: If tea and coffee are substitutes, a rise in the price of tea will:
options: har bir narxda kofega talabni kamaytiradi
har bir narxda kofega talabni oshiradi
kofe bozoriga mutlaqo ta'sir ko'rsatmaydi
har bir narxda kofe taklifini kamaytiradi
options_ru: снизит спрос на кофе при каждой цене
повысит спрос на кофе при каждой цене
никак не затронет рынок кофе в стране
снизит предложение кофе при каждой цене
options_en: reduce the demand for coffee at each price
raise the demand for coffee at each price
leave the coffee market entirely unaffected
reduce the supply of coffee at each price
questions.explanation_en: Substitutes satisfy the same need, so a higher price for one of them moves buyers towards the other and shifts its demand curve rightward. Option 0 describes the effect for complements, option 2 denies any relation, and option 3 confuses a demand shift with a supply shift.

questions.text_en: Cars and petrol are complements, so a sharp rise in the petrol price will:
options: har bir narxda avtomobilga talabni oshiradi
har bir narxda avtomobil taklifini oshiradi
avtomobilga talabni mutlaqo o'zgarmas qoldiradi
har bir narxda avtomobilga talabni kamaytiradi
options_ru: повысит спрос на автомобили при каждой цене
повысит предложение автомобилей при каждой цене
оставит спрос на автомобили совсем неизменным
снизит спрос на автомобили при каждой цене
options_en: increase the demand for cars at each price
increase the supply of cars at each price
leave the demand for cars entirely unchanged
decrease the demand for cars at each price
questions.explanation_en: Complements are consumed together, so a higher price of one raises the total cost of using the pair and shifts the demand for the other leftward. Option 0 describes substitutes, option 1 mistakes demand for supply, and option 2 denies the complementary relation.

questions.text_en: The law of supply states that, other things equal, quantity supplied:
options: tovarning bozor narxi oshgani sari ortadi
tovarning bozor narxi oshgani sari kamayadi
bozor narxidan butunlay mustaqil bo'ladi
birlik ishlab chiqarish xarajati oshsa ortadi
options_ru: растёт по мере роста рыночной цены блага
падает по мере роста рыночной цены блага
совершенно не зависит от рыночной цены
растёт по мере роста затрат на единицу
options_en: rises as the market price of the good rises
falls as the market price of the good rises
is independent of the market price entirely
rises as the production cost per unit rises
questions.explanation_en: A higher price makes production of extra units profitable, so quantity supplied rises and the supply curve slopes upward. Option 1 reverses the relation, option 2 describes a perfectly inelastic supply as a general law, and higher unit costs reduce rather than raise supply.

questions.text_en: Which of the following shifts the supply curve of a good?
options: Shu tovarning bozordagi narxidagi o'zgarish
Faqat tovar xaridorlari daromadidagi o'zgarish
Ishlatiladigan resurslar narxidagi o'zgarish
Tovar iste'molchilari didlaridagi o'zgarish
options_ru: Изменение цены этого блага на самом рынке
Изменение дохода лишь покупателей блага
Изменение цен используемых ресурсов блага
Изменение вкусов потребителей этого блага
options_en: A change in the price of that good on the market
A change in the income of the good's buyers only
A change in the prices of the inputs used in it
A change in the tastes of the good's consumers
questions.explanation_en: Supply shifts when non-price conditions of production change: input prices, technology, taxes and subsidies, the number of sellers and producers' expectations. The good's own price moves the economy along the supply curve, while buyers' income and tastes shift demand.

questions.text_en: An improvement in production technology will normally:
options: taklif chizig'ini chapga siljitib, narxni oshiradi
taklif chizig'ini o'ngga siljitib, narxni pasaytiradi
talab chizig'ini chapga siljitib, narxni pasaytiradi
ikki chiziqni ham aynan oldingi holatda qoldiradi
options_ru: сдвинет кривую предложения влево и поднимет цену
сдвинет кривую предложения вправо и снизит цену
сдвинет кривую спроса влево и тоже снизит цену
оставит обе кривые точно в прежних положениях
options_en: shift the supply curve to the left and raise price
shift the supply curve to the right and lower price
shift the demand curve to the left and lower price
leave both curves in exactly their former positions
questions.explanation_en: Better technology lowers unit costs, so firms are willing to offer more at every price; supply shifts right and, with unchanged demand, the equilibrium price falls while quantity rises. Technology does not shift demand and does not leave the market unchanged.

questions.text_en: A rise in the wages paid by firms in an industry will:
options: tarmoq talab chizig'ini o'ngga siljitadi
tarmoq taklif chizig'ini o'ngga siljitadi
tarmoq taklif chizig'ini joyida qoldiradi
tarmoq taklif chizig'ini chapga siljitadi
options_ru: сдвинет кривую спроса этой отрасли вправо
сдвинет кривую предложения отрасли вправо
оставит кривую предложения на прежнем месте
сдвинет кривую предложения отрасли влево
options_en: shift the industry demand curve to the right
shift the industry supply curve to the right
leave the industry supply curve where it was
shift the industry supply curve to the left
questions.explanation_en: Wages are an input price, so higher wages raise production costs and firms supply less at every price, shifting supply leftward and raising the equilibrium price. Option 1 reverses the direction, option 0 confuses supply with demand, and option 2 ignores the cost change.

questions.text_en: Market equilibrium is the situation in which:
options: bozor narxi mahsulotning o'rtacha xarajatiga teng bo'ladi
har bir ishlab chiqaruvchi birlikdan bir xil foyda oladi
ma'lum narxda talab miqdori taklif miqdoriga teng bo'ladi
davlat ikki tomon uchun maqbul narxni belgilab beradi
options_ru: рыночная цена равна средним издержкам выпуска
каждый производитель имеет равную прибыль с единицы
величина спроса равна величине предложения при цене
государство задаёт цену, приемлемую для двух сторон
options_en: the market price equals the average cost of output
every producer earns the same profit per unit sold
quantity demanded equals quantity supplied at a price
the state sets a price acceptable to both sides
questions.explanation_en: Equilibrium is the price-quantity combination at which the plans of buyers and sellers coincide, so there is neither shortage nor surplus and no tendency for price to change. Equality of price and average cost is a long-run competitive condition, equal profits are not required, and administered prices are not market equilibrium.

questions.text_en: If the market price is set above the equilibrium level, there will be:
options: tanqislik, chunki xaridorlar taklifdan ko'proq talab qiladi
ortiqchalik, chunki sotuvchilar talabdan ko'proq taklif qiladi
muvozanatsizlik bo'lmaydi, chunki chiziqlar darhol siljiydi
amalda ayirboshlangan miqdorning doimiy ortib borishi
options_ru: дефицит, так как покупатели хотят больше, чем предложено
излишек, так как продавцы предлагают больше, чем нужно
отсутствие дисбаланса, ведь кривые сдвинутся мгновенно
постоянный рост фактически обмениваемого количества
options_en: a shortage, since buyers want more than is offered
a surplus, since sellers offer more than is wanted
no imbalance, because the curves will shift at once
a permanent rise in the quantity actually traded
questions.explanation_en: Above equilibrium, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, so unsold stocks accumulate and competition among sellers pushes the price back down. A shortage arises at prices below equilibrium, the curves themselves do not move, and traded quantity falls rather than rises.

questions.text_en: If the market price is held below the equilibrium level, the result is:
options: tovar tanqisligi va qoniqmagan xaridorlar navbati
tovar ortiqchaligi va sotilmagan zaxiralar o'sishi
talab chizig'ining darhol chapga siljib ketishi
har bir sotuvchi oladigan foydaning ko'payishi
options_ru: дефицит блага и очереди неудовлетворённых покупателей
излишек блага и растущие непроданные его запасы
немедленный сдвиг кривой спроса влево на графике
увеличение прибыли, получаемой каждым продавцом
options_en: a shortage of the good and queues of unsatisfied buyers
a surplus of the good and growing unsold stocks of it
an immediate shift of the demand curve to the left
an increase in the profit earned by every seller
questions.explanation_en: Below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, producing shortages, queues and non-price rationing. A surplus appears only above equilibrium, the demand curve does not shift, and sellers' profits fall rather than rise at an artificially low price.

questions.text_en: If demand increases while supply stays unchanged, the equilibrium:
options: narx pasayadi va muvozanat miqdori ham kamayadi
narx oshadi, muvozanat miqdori esa kamayib boradi
narx pasayadi, muvozanat miqdori esa ortib boradi
narx oshadi va muvozanat miqdori ham ortib boradi
options_ru: цена падает, и равновесное количество тоже падает
цена растёт, а равновесное количество при этом падает
цена падает, а равновесное количество при этом растёт
цена растёт, и равновесное количество тоже возрастает
options_en: price falls and the equilibrium quantity also falls
price rises while the equilibrium quantity falls
price falls while the equilibrium quantity rises
price rises and the equilibrium quantity also rises
questions.explanation_en: A rightward shift of demand along an unchanged upward-sloping supply curve raises both the equilibrium price and the equilibrium quantity. The other combinations correspond to a fall in demand, a fall in supply, and a rise in supply respectively.

questions.text_en: If supply increases while demand stays unchanged, the equilibrium:
options: narx oshadi va muvozanat miqdori ham ortib boradi
narx oshadi, muvozanat miqdori esa kamayib boradi
narx pasayadi, muvozanat miqdori esa ortib boradi
narx pasayadi va muvozanat miqdori ham kamayadi
options_ru: цена растёт, и равновесное количество тоже возрастает
цена растёт, а равновесное количество при этом падает
цена падает, а равновесное количество при этом растёт
цена падает, и равновесное количество тоже падает
options_en: price rises and the equilibrium quantity also rises
price rises while the equilibrium quantity falls
price falls while the equilibrium quantity rises
price falls and the equilibrium quantity also falls
questions.explanation_en: A rightward shift of supply along an unchanged downward-sloping demand curve lowers the equilibrium price and raises the equilibrium quantity. Option 0 describes a demand increase, option 1 a supply decrease, and option 3 a demand decrease.

questions.text_en: If both demand and supply increase at the same time, then:
options: narx albatta oshadi, miqdor esa albatta kamayadi
miqdor albatta ortadi, narx esa aniqlanmagan bo'ladi
narx albatta pasayadi va miqdor ham albatta kamayadi
miqdor albatta kamayadi, narx esa albatta oshadi
options_ru: цена непременно растёт, а количество непременно падает
количество непременно растёт, а цена неопределённа
цена непременно падает, и количество тоже падает
количество непременно падает, а цена точно растёт
options_en: price certainly rises and quantity certainly falls
quantity certainly rises while price is indeterminate
price certainly falls and quantity certainly falls
quantity certainly falls while price surely rises
questions.explanation_en: Both shifts raise equilibrium quantity, so quantity definitely increases, but they push price in opposite directions, so the price change depends on the relative size of the two shifts. The other options claim a definite price result that the analysis does not support.

questions.text_en: A price ceiling set below the equilibrium price typically produces:
options: doimiy tanqislik va qora bozorlarning o'sib borishi
doimiy ortiqchalik va sotilmagan katta tovar zaxirasi
barcha sotuvchilar foydasining darhol ko'tarilishi
o'sha mahsulotga talabning butunlay yo'q bo'lib ketishi
options_ru: устойчивый дефицит и рост чёрных рынков данного блага
устойчивый излишек и большие непроданные запасы блага
немедленный рост прибыли у всех продавцов этого блага
полное исчезновение спроса на этот самый продукт рынка
options_en: a persistent shortage and the growth of black markets
a persistent surplus and large unsold stocks of goods
an immediate rise in the profits of all the sellers
a complete disappearance of demand for that product
questions.explanation_en: A binding maximum price keeps quantity demanded above quantity supplied, so shortages persist and goods are rationed by queues or informal markets. Surpluses follow from price floors, sellers' profits are squeezed, and demand does not disappear but exceeds supply.

questions.text_en: A minimum price (price floor) fixed above equilibrium normally causes:
options: tanqislik, chunki xaridorlar kam tovar uchun kurashadi
bozordagi miqdorlarning bir-biriga aniq muvozanatlashuvi
ortiqchalik, chunki sotuvchilar xaridlardan ko'p taklif qiladi
ishlab chiqaruvchi firmalar xarajatlarining pasayishi
options_ru: дефицит, так как покупателям не хватает блага
точное равенство количеств на этом самом рынке
излишек, так как продавцы предлагают больше покупок
снижение издержек, несомых производящими фирмами
options_en: a shortage, as buyers compete for too few goods
an exact balance of the quantities on the market
a surplus, as sellers offer more than is bought
a fall in the costs borne by producing firms
questions.explanation_en: A binding minimum price keeps quantity supplied above quantity demanded, which is why agricultural price support schemes generate stocks that the state must buy up. Shortages come from price ceilings, the market does not clear under a binding floor, and production costs are unaffected.

questions.text_en: Price elasticity of demand is calculated as the ratio of:
options: narx o'zgarishining talab miqdori o'zgarishiga nisbati
miqdor foiz o'zgarishining narx foiz o'zgarishiga nisbati
umumiy tushumning sotilgan tovar umumiy miqdoriga nisbati
talab qilingan miqdorning taklif qilingan miqdorga nisbati
options_ru: изменения цены к изменению величины спроса на благо
процентного изменения количества к изменению цены
общей выручки к общему проданному количеству блага
величины спроса к величине предложения этого блага
options_en: the change in price to the change in quantity demanded
the percentage change in quantity to that in price
total revenue to the total quantity of the good sold
the quantity demanded to the quantity supplied of it
questions.explanation_en: Elasticity is a ratio of relative (percentage) changes, Ed = (%change in Q) / (%change in P), which makes it independent of measurement units. Option 0 inverts the ratio and uses absolute changes, option 2 defines average revenue, and option 3 is a disequilibrium ratio.

questions.text_en: Demand for a good is called elastic when the absolute value of its elasticity is:
options: chiziqning har bir nuqtasida aynan nolga teng
nol va bir orasida, demak miqdor kuchsiz javob beradi
butun talab chizig'i bo'ylab aynan birga teng bo'ladi
birdan katta, demak miqdor kuchli javob beradi
options_ru: в точности равна нулю в каждой точке кривой
между нулём и единицей, спрос реагирует слабо
в точности равна единице по всей кривой спроса
больше единицы, спрос реагирует очень сильно
options_en: exactly equal to zero at every point of the curve
between zero and one, so quantity reacts weakly
exactly equal to one along the whole demand curve
greater than one, so quantity reacts strongly
questions.explanation_en: Demand is elastic when |Ed| > 1, meaning quantity changes proportionally more than price. A value between zero and one is inelastic demand, a value of one is unit elasticity, and zero is perfectly inelastic demand.

questions.text_en: Perfectly inelastic demand is represented graphically by:
options: qat'iy talab miqdorida vertikal chiziq bilan
qat'iy bozor narxida gorizontal chiziq bilan
qiyaligi aynan minus birga teng chiziq bilan
chapdan o'ngga keskin ko'tariluvchi chiziq bilan
options_ru: вертикальной линией при фиксированном количестве
горизонтальной линией при фиксированной цене блага
кривой с наклоном, в точности равным минус единице
линией, круто поднимающейся слева направо вверх
options_en: a vertical line at a fixed quantity demanded
a horizontal line at a fixed market price
a curve with a slope of exactly minus one
a line rising steeply from left to right
questions.explanation_en: If quantity demanded does not react to price at all, the demand curve is vertical and elasticity equals zero. A horizontal line is perfectly elastic demand, a slope of minus one is not the same as unit elasticity, and an upward-sloping line would contradict the law of demand.

questions.text_en: Which factor makes the demand for a good more price-elastic?
options: Tovar o'rnini bosuvchisi yo'q zaruriy mahsulot bo'lsa
Tovar xaridor budjetining juda kichik ulushini olsa
Tovarning yaqin o'rnini bosuvchilari oson topilsa
Xaridor xaridni darhol hal qilishi shart bo'lsa
options_ru: Благо является насущным и не имеет заменителей
Благо занимает крошечную долю бюджета покупателя
Близкие заменители блага легко доступны на рынке
Покупатель должен решить о покупке немедленно же
options_en: The good is an urgent necessity with no substitutes
The good takes a tiny share of the buyer's budget
Close substitutes for the good are easily available
The buyer must decide on the purchase immediately
questions.explanation_en: The availability of close substitutes is the strongest source of elasticity, since buyers can easily switch away when the price rises. Necessities without substitutes, goods with a small budget share, and purchases that cannot be postponed all tend to have inelastic demand.

questions.text_en: If demand for a good is price-elastic, a reduction in its price will:
options: sotuvchilar oladigan umumiy tushumni kamaytiradi
sotuvchilar oladigan umumiy tushumni oshiradi
sotuvchilar umumiy tushumini o'zgarmas qoldiradi
sotuvchilar birlik xarajatini oshirib yuboradi
options_ru: уменьшит общую выручку, получаемую продавцами
увеличит общую выручку, получаемую продавцами
оставит общую выручку продавцов неизменной же
повысит затраты продавцов на единицу товара
options_en: reduce the total revenue received by the sellers
raise the total revenue received by the sellers
leave the total revenue of the sellers unchanged
raise the total cost per unit borne by sellers
questions.explanation_en: With elastic demand the percentage rise in quantity exceeds the percentage fall in price, so total revenue (P times Q) increases. Revenue would fall if demand were inelastic, stay constant only at unit elasticity, and a price cut does not change unit production costs.

questions.text_en: For two substitute goods, the cross elasticity of demand is:
options: musbat, chunki narxlar talabni bir yo'nalishda harakatlantiradi
manfiy, chunki narx o'sishi boshqasiga talabni kamaytiradi
narxlar qanday bo'lishidan qat'i nazar doimo nolga teng
aniqlanmagan, chunki o'rin bosuvchilarni qiyoslab bo'lmaydi
options_ru: положительной, ведь цены двигают спрос в одну сторону
отрицательной, ведь рост цены снижает спрос на другое
всегда равной нулю, какими бы ни оказались цены благ
неопределённой, ведь заменители нельзя сопоставлять
options_en: positive, since the two prices move demand together
negative, since a price rise cuts the other demand
always equal to zero whatever the prices may be
undefined, because substitutes cannot be compared
questions.explanation_en: For substitutes a rise in the price of one good raises demand for the other, so cross elasticity is positive. A negative value indicates complements, a value of zero indicates unrelated goods, and the coefficient is always computable.

questions.text_en: The price elasticity of supply is usually greater when:
options: firmada bo'sh ishlab chiqarish quvvati umuman bo'lmasa
tovar uchun resurslarni boshqa olishning imkoni bo'lmasa
faqat juda qisqa vaqt davri ko'rib chiqilayotgan bo'lsa
firmalarga moslashish uchun uzoqroq davr mavjud bo'lsa
options_ru: у фирмы вовсе нет свободных производственных мощностей
ресурсы для блага больше невозможно нигде приобрести
рассматривается только очень короткий период времени
у фирм есть более длительный период приспособления
options_en: the firm has no spare production capacity at all
inputs for the good cannot be obtained any more
only a very short period of time is considered
a longer period of adjustment is available to firms
questions.explanation_en: Time is the key determinant of supply elasticity: in the long run firms can change capacity, hire more inputs and enter or leave the industry, so quantity responds strongly to price. Absent capacity, unavailable inputs and very short periods all make supply inelastic.

questions.text_en: Which feature best characterizes a perfectly competitive market?
options: Ko'plab mayda firmalar, har biri narx oluvchi
Bitta yirik sotuvchi bozor narxini belgilaydi
Bir nechta yirik firma bir-biriga qaraydi
Ko'p firma bir-biridan farqli tovar sotadi
options_ru: Множество мелких фирм, каждая принимает цену
Один крупный продавец сам устанавливает цену
Несколько крупных фирм реагируют друг на друга
Много фирм продают слегка разные товары
options_en: Many small firms, each acting as a price taker
One large seller that chooses the market price
A few large firms that react to each other
Many firms selling slightly different goods
questions.explanation_en: Perfect competition requires many small firms selling a homogeneous good, so each is a price taker. A single price-setting seller is monopoly, mutual reaction defines oligopoly, and product differentiation defines monopolistic competition.

questions.text_en: The demand curve facing an individual firm in perfect competition is
options: firma quvvati hajmida vertikal shaklda
resurs tanqisligi tufayli o'suvchi chiziq
amaldagi bozor narxi darajasida gorizontal
butun bozor doirasida pasayib boruvchi
options_ru: вертикальной на уровне мощности фирмы
возрастающей из-за дефицита ресурсов
горизонтальной на уровне рыночной цены
убывающей на всем рыночном диапазоне
options_en: vertical at the firm's capacity output
upward sloping because of scarce inputs
horizontal at the prevailing market price
downward sloping over the whole market range
questions.explanation_en: The individual firm can sell any quantity at the going price, so its demand curve is horizontal (perfectly elastic). The downward-sloping curve is the market demand curve, not the single firm's.

questions.text_en: For a price-taking firm, marginal revenue is equal to
options: tanlangan hajmdagi o'rtacha xarajatga
mahsulotning amaldagi bozor narxiga
olingan umumiy tushumning yarmiga
umumiy xarajat chizig'i qiyaligiga
options_ru: средним издержкам при этом объеме
рыночной цене данного продукта
половине полученной общей выручки
наклону кривой общих издержек
options_en: average cost at the chosen output
the market price of the product
half of the total revenue earned
the slope of the total cost curve
questions.explanation_en: Because price is constant for a price taker, each extra unit adds exactly the price to revenue, so MR = P. The slope of total cost is marginal cost, and average cost is a cost concept, not revenue.

questions.text_en: A firm maximizes profit by producing the output at which
options: o'rtacha xarajat eng past nuqtaga tushadi
umumiy tushum eng yuqori darajaga chiqadi
narx o'rtacha xarajatdan eng ko'p oshadi
chekli tushum chekli xarajatga tenglashadi
options_ru: средние общие издержки достигают минимума
общая выручка достигает своего максимума
цена максимально превышает средние издержки
предельная выручка равна предельным издержкам
options_en: average cost reaches its lowest point
total revenue reaches its highest level
the price exceeds average cost the most
marginal revenue equals marginal cost
questions.explanation_en: Profit is maximised where MR = MC. Minimising average cost or maximising total revenue ignores the trade-off between extra revenue and extra cost, and maximising the price-cost gap per unit ignores quantity.

questions.text_en: In long-run equilibrium under perfect competition, each firm
options: omon qolish uchun narxni MC dan yuqori qo'yadi
xarajati minimal hajmdan kamroq ishlab chiqaradi
minimal ATC da nol iqtisodiy foyda oladi
katta va juda barqaror iqtisodiy foyda oladi
options_ru: держит цену выше предельных издержек ради выживания
выпускает меньше объема, минимизирующего издержки
получает нулевую экономическую прибыль при min ATC
получает большую стабильную экономическую прибыль
options_en: sets price above marginal cost to survive
produces below the level that minimises cost
earns zero economic profit at minimum ATC
earns a large and stable economic profit
questions.explanation_en: Free entry and exit drive price to minimum average total cost, so economic profit is zero (only normal profit remains). Positive long-run profit would attract entry; price above MC is a feature of market power.

questions.text_en: A competitive firm should shut down in the short run when price falls below
options: shu hajmdagi o'rtacha umumiy xarajatdan
shu hajmdagi o'rtacha doimiy xarajatdan
shu hajm darajasidagi chekli xarajatdan
shu hajmdagi o'rtacha o'zgaruvchi xarajatdan
options_ru: средних общих издержек при этом объеме
средних постоянных издержек при этом объеме
предельных издержек при данном объеме
средних переменных издержек при этом объеме
options_en: its average total cost at that output
its average fixed cost at that output
its marginal cost at that output level
its average variable cost at that output
questions.explanation_en: If price cannot cover average variable cost, producing adds more to variable cost than to revenue, so stopping limits the loss to fixed cost. Below average total cost but above AVC the firm still operates in the short run.

questions.text_en: A pure monopoly is a market in which
options: bitta firma o'rinbosari yo'q tovarni taklif qiladi
ikki firma bozor savdosining deyarli barchasini oladi
ko'p firma bir xil standart tovarni taklif qiladi
ko'p firma tabaqalashgan brendli tovar taklif qiladi
options_ru: одна фирма поставляет товар без близких заменителей
две фирмы делят почти все продажи на этом рынке
много фирм поставляют одинаковый стандартный товар
много фирм поставляют разные брендированные товары
options_en: one firm supplies a good with no close substitutes
two firms share nearly all of the market sales
many firms supply a standardised, identical good
many firms supply branded, differentiated goods
questions.explanation_en: Monopoly means a single seller of a product with no close substitutes, protected by entry barriers. Two dominant firms form a duopoly, identical goods with many sellers is perfect competition, and branded variety is monopolistic competition.

questions.text_en: For a monopolist facing a downward-sloping demand curve, marginal revenue is
options: hajmga bog'liq bo'lmagan doimiy miqdor
har bir birlik narxidan kichik bo'ladi
har bir birlik narxiga teng bo'ladi
har bir birlik narxidan katta bo'ladi
options_ru: постоянна и не зависит от объема продаж
меньше цены, установленной за единицу
равна цене, установленной за единицу
больше цены, установленной за единицу
options_en: constant and independent of output sold
less than the price charged on each unit
equal to the price charged on each unit
greater than the price charged per unit
